learning_outcomes.text: Applies correctly the principles of thermodynamics and heat transfer to the resolution of engineering problems.
Applies heat transfer knowledge in the calculation and design of heat exchangers.

Recognizes the different forms of heat transfer and the cases in which each of them is relevant. Solves heat transfer problems involving mechanisms acting in series and/or parallel. Identifies the type of convection and calculates the convection coefficient using correlations.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts and basic modalities of heat transfer.
Electrical analogy. Heat transfer mechanisms in series and parallel.
One-dimensional steady-state conduction without heat generation.
Steady-state conduction without heat generation. Planar, cylindrical, and spherical geometry.
Conduction in a body of null thermal resistance.
Conduction in one-dimensional systems. Solution of two-dimensional and three-dimensional systems as a product of one-dimensional solutions.
Dimensionless parameters for the correlation of convection data.
Heat transfer in boiling and condensation.
Selection criteria. Selection among possible options.
Efficiency of heat exchangers. NTU method for the design and analysis of a heat exchanger.
Kern method for the calculation of shell and tube exchangers without phase change.
Introduction. Physical aspects of electromagnetic radiation.
Black body radiation, Planck, Wien and Stefan-Boltzmann laws.
Surface emission. Surface absorption, reflection and transmission.
View factors. Relationship between view factors.
teaching_methods: Problem-solving/exercise sessions in the ordinary classroom

assessment_methods.method: Problem-solving/exercises in the ordinary classroom (2 problems to be submitted solved in groups)

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 3.5 is required for averaging with the first partial exam and the group exercises. For the second attempt (resit), the exam will cover the entire subject matter, and the exam score will constitute 100% of the final grade. The fraudulent use of any means, including AI, in evaluative activities will result in a failing grade for that activity.
